name: Illinois

jury_list.statute: No section of the Jury Act (705 ILCS 305) opens or closes records of persons found not qualified as non-citizens. 705 ILCS 305/2(a)(4): jurors must be 'Citizens of the United States of America.' 305/8: if the clerk draws the name of a person who 'is legally disqualified to serve as a juror, the clerk shall report the name of such person to the county clerk'. Status: null.
jury_list.holder: Circuit court clerks, county clerks (jury box, 705 ILCS 305/7), and jury commissions or jury administrators under the Jury Commission Act (705 ILCS 310).
jury_list.official_pipeline: 705 ILCS 305/8: 'should the clerk draw from the box the name of a person who is known to be dead, to have been selected as a grand juror, a non-resident, absent from the State, unable to attend in consequence of illness, or that he is legally disqualified to serve as a juror, the clerk shall report the name of such person to the county clerk, and the clerk of such court shall draw other names until the required number have been selected'. The statute sends the names of legally disqualified persons to the county clerk. It does not mention citizenship or voter-list use.

sources.cite: 705 ILCS 305/1 (jury list drawn from voter, driver's license and ID card, and unemployment claimant lists)
705 ILCS 305/8 (names of drawn persons who are legally disqualified are reported to the county clerk)

voter_file.who_may_get: Electronic voter data goes only to political committees and governmental entities. Any person may view the statewide list on a screen at the State Board of Elections in Springfield (not in the 27 days before an election) but may not print, duplicate, transmit, or alter it (10 ILCS 5/4-8).
voter_file.permitted_uses: Bona fide political purposes, under sworn affidavit by the committee representative; never for commercial solicitation or other business purposes (10 ILCS 5/4-8).
voter_file.use_restriction: 10 ILCS 5/4-8: 'The individual representing a political committee requesting copies of such tapes shall make a sworn affidavit that the information shall be used only for bona fide political purposes, including by or for candidates for office or incumbent office holders. Such tapes, discs or other electronic data shall not be used under any circumstances by any political committee or individuals for purposes of commercial solicitation or other business purposes.'
voter_file.penalty: Class 4 felony for commercial or business use (10 ILCS 5/4-8).
voter_file.attestation_required: Sworn affidavit by a political committee representative that the data will be used only for bona fide political purposes (10 ILCS 5/4-8).

private_challenge.who: Any voter in the township, city, village, or town containing the precinct, and any precinct committeeperson in the county (10 ILCS 5/4-12; 5/5-15 for other counties).
private_challenge.form_or_statute: 10 ILCS 5/4-12: sworn application to the county clerk to erase a name from the precinct register, in the statutory form, stating the reason; notice and a show-cause hearing follow.
private_challenge.deadlines: Filed only on Monday and Tuesday of the second week before the week of the election (10 ILCS 5/4-12). For the November 3, 2026 election that is October 19-20, 2026.
private_challenge.evidence_standard: Affiant swears 'that he has personal knowledge of the facts set forth in the above affidavit' (statutory form, 10 ILCS 5/4-12).
private_challenge.false_statement_penalty: Sworn before the county clerk (perjury law applies; penalty not stated in 4-12).

sources.cite: 10 ILCS 5/5-15 (same procedure in counties under Article 5)

state_windows.applies_to: Applications to erase names under 10 ILCS 5/4-12
state_windows.effect: Filing is allowed only on Monday and Tuesday of the second week before the election week (about 14-15 days before).

county_board.name: Illinois election authorities list (State Board of Elections)
county_board.note: Applications under 4-12 go to the county clerk or board of election commissioners.

audit_path.statute: 5 ILCS 140 (Freedom of Information Act) and 52 U.S.C. 20507(i) (NVRA public inspection of list-maintenance records)
audit_path.what_you_can_request: Counts only, from the county clerk: per year, the number of reports of legally disqualified drawn jurors received under 705 ILCS 305/8, and the number of any voter-list actions that resulted. From the county clerk or board of election commissioners: per year, the number of registrations cancelled because the registrant was not a U.S. citizen, and the number of applications filed under 10 ILCS 5/4-12 (or 5-15, 6-35) on that ground.
audit_path.note: Do not ask for names. 705 ILCS 305/8 sends the names of legally disqualified persons to the county clerk. It does not mention citizenship or voter-list use, so the letter must not say a non-citizen pipeline exists. Whether FOIA reaches court jury records was not confirmed.

gates.basis: Jury records: no Illinois statute opens or closes records of non-citizen disqualifications (null), so counts only. Illinois allows a sworn application on personal knowledge in a two-day window (10 ILCS 5/4-12). Private persons cannot get electronic voter data (5/4-8). Strict gates.

No voter_file value changes. 2026-10-07 (Optimus final rulings, REQ-NOTE 65): voter_file.use_restriction added with the exact statutory text (filled from the statute); the app shows it and requires the user's attestation before the voter file loads.

CHANGED 2026-10-07 14:39 (user ruling on REQ-NOTE 41): official_pipeline null to an exact quote of 705 ILCS 305/8. The statute sends the names of legally disqualified persons to the county clerk. It does not mention citizenship or voter-list use. Behavior flag: the A.5 audit letter now runs for IL. It may ask the county clerk for counts of disqualified-juror reports received and any resulting voter-list actions, but it must not claim a non-citizen pipeline exists (REQ-NOTE 45). In many counties the county clerk is also the election authority; the statute does not say so.

PA-style check: no Illinois statute makes a list of non-citizen jury disqualifications public. 305/7 keeps the list of selected jurors in the county clerk's office but says nothing about public inspection.
Private persons cannot lawfully obtain an Illinois voter file; they may only view it on screen in Springfield (10 ILCS 5/4-8). JuryRoll cannot be used lawfully by most Illinois private users.
Cancelled-voter file: no published Illinois cancelled-voter file with a jury reason code was found. REQ-NOTE 27 drops cancelled rows before matching.
The 4-12 affidavit requires personal knowledge. A data match alone is unlikely to qualify.
Article 6 (boards of election commissioners) has a parallel procedure that was not read in this batch.
one_per_affidavit is true: the statutory form names one person.
